title: Pure-tensor normalized ordinary scalar balancing at one quotient level
statement: Fix a prime ell, finite Q_ell extensions E and F, a Q_ell algebra map i:E→F, a scheme W, and e≥1 satisfying the ramification ideal equality of [def-pur-finite-compact-support-scalar-data]. Use constant scalar tensor from [def-pur-constant-scalar-tensor-data] and the ordinary quotient/limit adjunction of [def-pur-native-reduction-counit-data]. For every completed E-module sheaf M and positive level n+1, there exists an isomorphism from B tensor_A the nth ordinary E-reduction of M to the ordinary F-reduction at e(n+1) of completed scalar extension of M. Its value on every local section b tensor eta_E(x) is eta_F(c_F(b) tensor x), where eta is the adjunction unit followed by its limit projection and c_F is the fixed constant-to-completion map. There is no assertion about naturality in M or horizontal indices, nor uniqueness of the isomorphism.

source.place: lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict (Tag 03EK), section-tensor-product; sites-cohomology.tex section-derived-limits (Tag 0940). Single-level quotient algebra and local generation in the original ordinaryBalancing_existsUnique docstring.

proof.text: Evaluation of the ordinary quotient-system left adjoint is ordinary sheafified quotient extension at the given level. Its unit is induced by the quotient projection: construct the quotient tower on each module and use the tensor/restriction adjunction and diagonal/limit adjunction to compare with the specified left adjoint, preserving units.

Ramification implies that the extension of (t^(n+1)) is (v^(e(n+1))). The finite-free identification of completed coefficient extension gives B tensor_A Ahat = Bhat. Tensor reassociation and the tensor/quotient equivalence produce the displayed single-level isomorphism. Its forward map takes b tensor (1 tensor x) to 1 tensor (c_F(b) tensor x); reverse reassociation is its inverse. Verify the two composites on tensor generators.

The balanced maps commute with site restrictions and descend through module sheafification. The preceding unit-preserving comparison makes the formula exactly the specified adjunction-unit formula. Positivity identifies e(n+1)-1+1 with e(n+1). This construction does not assume naturality of the selected witnesses in M or n.

theorem ordinaryScalarBalancingLevel_exists (W : Scheme.{u}) (e : ℕ)
    (he : PurCompactSupport.Ramification l E F i e) (hepos : 1 ≤ e) :
    let ηE (M : scalarReductionSource l E W) (n : ℕ) (U : W.ProEtᵒᵖ)
        (x : M.val.obj U) :=
      (((ordinaryReductionAdj l E W).unit.app M ≫
        limit.π ((coefficientSequenceRestriction.{u, u} l E W).obj
          ((ordinaryReduction l E W).obj M)) (op n)).val.app U) x
    let ηF (M : scalarReductionSource l F W) (n : ℕ) (U : W.ProEtᵒᵖ)
        (x : M.val.obj U) :=
      (((ordinaryReductionAdj l F W).unit.app M ≫
        limit.π ((coefficientSequenceRestriction.{u, u} l F W).obj
          ((ordinaryReduction l F W).obj M)) (op n)).val.app U) x
    ∀ (M : scalarReductionSource l E W) (n : ℕ),
    ∃ β : (pbcExtend (constantMap l E F i W)).obj
        (((ordinaryReduction l E W ⋙ systemRestriction l E W).obj M).obj (op n)) ≅
      (((ordinaryReduction l F W ⋙ systemRestriction l F W).obj
        ((pbcExtend (completedCoefficientMap l E F i W)).obj M)).obj
          (op (e * (n + 1) - 1))),
      ∀ (U : W.ProEtᵒᵖ)
        (b : ((constants l F).ring W).obj.obj U) (x : M.val.obj U),
        (β.hom.val.app U)
            (pbcTensorSection (constantMap l E F i W)
              ((((ordinaryReduction l E W ⋙ systemRestriction l E W)).obj M).obj (op n)) U b
              (ηE M n U x)) =
          ηF
            ((pbcExtend (completedCoefficientMap l E F i W)).obj M)
            (e * (n + 1) - 1) U
            (pbcTensorSection (completedCoefficientMap l E F i W) M U
              (((integralConstantToCompletionOfUniverses l F W).hom.app U) b) x)
